title: Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan Collectibles and Art Cap on Reconsidered Claims
content:
On a reconsideration of a Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan claim, the collectibles value is capped at the reconsideration's collectibles cap.

**Re-assessment.** A new document can bring a fresh adjuster assessment, and the claim is re-assessed when its latest adjuster assessment is dated after the latest decision on the claim.

**The cap.** The reconsideration's collectibles cap is the level's collectibles and art sublimit multiplied by 1.5 when the claim is re-assessed and the covered unit's class holds humidity control, by 1.25 when the claim is re-assessed and the class holds a temperature band but no humidity control, and by 1 otherwise. The climate features are those of the unit class of the covered Self-Storage Unit Rental Agreement; the dates are those of the assessment and decision entries in the claim's handling history.

| Latest adjuster assessment dated after the latest decision | Unit class humidity control | Unit class temperature band | Reconsideration's collectibles cap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | held | any | sublimit multiplied by 1.5 |
| yes | none | held | sublimit multiplied by 1.25 |
| yes | none | not controlled | sublimit multiplied by 1 |
| no | any | any | sublimit multiplied by 1 |

**Points of judgement.** "Dated after" compares the two dates in the claim's handling history: an assessment dated the same day as the latest decision, or earlier, does not make the claim re-assessed.

*Illustration (hypothetical):* with a collectibles sublimit of 2,200.00, a re-assessed claim in a unit class holding humidity control has a cap of 3,300.00; a re-assessed claim in a class with a temperature band only, 2,750.00; a claim whose latest assessment predates its latest decision, 2,200.00 whatever the class.
